sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Setup and company search
sections.what: Sets up the entry routes and the company search, which returns up to 25 company names matching at least two letters, each with a count of projects. Also starts the project lookup, which checks the industry and searches project names with escaped wildcards. Errors return a plain message.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the user find the largest companies first, since results are sorted by project count.
sections.watch_out: Company search reads every project on each request, so it may slow down as the table grows.

sections.name: File setup: if
sections.title: Project lookup with web research fallback
sections.what: If the named project is already in the Yard, it returns that project's stored details and stored source links. If not, it runs a web search, reads up to five pages, and proposes peer projects from the same industry, stating clearly that no Yard record exists.
sections.why: Lets the analyst look up a project the Yard does not hold, while refusing to invent facts when research fails.
sections.watch_out: Peer matching depends on segment names appearing in the fetched text, so a failed fetch can change which peers are shown. The end of the summary text was cut off in what was provided, so its exact wording could not be checked here.

summary: Provides the entry web addresses for company search and project lookup. Only the first part of the file was visible.
purpose: Lets a user find a company or a project by name before starting a scan.
why: Likely reason: a scan needs a company or project to start from, and the search keeps the list short.
how: 1. Company search: needs at least two letters, scans every project for matching company names, groups them, sorts by number of projects, and returns up to 25. 2. Project lookup: checks the request and the industry code, then searches project names for up to 10 matches. The rest of the file was not visible.
inputs: A search text for company search. For project lookup, a project name and an industry code.
outputs: A list of company names with project counts. For project lookup, matching project rows, as far as the visible code shows.
risks: Company search reads every project on each request. The project lookup escapes wildcard characters in the name. The remainder of the file, which holds the rest of the lookup, was not visible, so its risks cannot be checked.
debug: If company search returns nothing, check the query has at least two letters and that the operator or party role matches. If lookup returns a 400 error, check the industry code.
